api/generated/SmartDock.DockManager.html.summary: Class DockManager Namespace SmartDock Assembly SmartDock.dll Hosts a DockLayout. Register content by id, assign Layout, and the control builds the splits, tabs, floating windows, and auto-hide bars. Only the selected tab's content is in the tree. Drag a tab along its strip to reorder it, or off the strip to float it, then drop it on a guide to dock it. A tool, or a float of tools, can also drop on an auto-hide strip. Guides and the landing preview are drawn in a topmost overlay so the dragged window cannot cover them. Another float under the pointer shows that float's compass and edge guides; the topmost one wins, and the dragged window is skipped. A dock guide or that float wins where it overlaps an auto-hide hot zone. Documents are not an auto-hide target. The same gesture is covered by the internal drag methods, which call DockDragSession with coordinates and no mouse. Ctrl+Tab switches panes. DockCommands closes, cycles document tabs, and toggles float and auto-hide. When AnimationsEnabled is set and Windows animations are on, reordered tab headers slide and the dock guides fade. The auto-hide flyout is a child window so it paints above an HwndHost pane. It opens and closes at its arranged size: a render transform does not move that HWND. Those clocks do not change layout, focus, or events. ResizeGripThickness is the hit zone of a splitter, a flyout edge, and a float's border. ResizeMode applies splitter, flyout, and floating-window sizes live, once per frame, or as a preview on release. public sealed class DockManager : Border, IAnimatable, ISupportInitialize, Leaving the tray undocks it into a floating window while the button is still held. Double-click docks a floating toolbar back to the band it left. The default template paints three dots with Dock.Muted on Dock.Chrome. DockToolBarItem Bindable properties for one toolbar in ToolBarsSource. A Style assigned to ToolBarItemStyle targets this type. Its setters bind against the item, which is the DataContext. The manager reads these values when the toolbar enters the source and again when they change. This element is not placed in the visual tree. DockToolBarTray One edge of the dock that hosts toolbar bands. The template's PART_Bands panel receives one child per band. The default template fills Dock.Chrome. DockTree Short constructors for a layout tree. The same tree can be built with object initializers or XAML. DragPointer Reused pointer state for DockDragSession. Fill Leaves and Headers in place so a drag move does not allocate those lists. FloatWindow A floating window. Coordinates are device-independent pixels. HiddenEntry A pane Hide(DockLayout, string) took out of the tree, plus the place Show(DockLayout, string) returns it to. Default place fields are omitted from JSON. LayoutMap Resolves a layout to content ids. Pass the ids the application can create and the map reports which saved panes have no factory (MissingContentIds) and which factories the layout does not use (UnplacedContentIds). Both of those lists are sorted. Panels follows the visible tree: main, then floating windows, then auto-hide edges. Hidden panes are not listed. A known id that is only hidden is not unplaced. An unknown hidden id is missing. SplitChild One cell of a SplitNode. SplitNode A resizable split. Proportions are positive weights, not required to sum to 1. TabGroupNode A tabbed group of panes. The selected index is part of the saved layout. TabStrip Header geometry for a tab strip, in the same coordinates as the pointer. ToolBarBands Hit testing and placement for toolbar bands. The host measures the trays and passes the rectangles. Hit(DockRect, string, ReadOnlySpan<ToolBarBarRect>, ReadOnlySpan<ToolBarBandRect>, ReadOnlySpan<ToolBarTrayRect>, double, double, string, string) does not allocate. ToolBarCustomizationEventArgs The toolbar and button a customization change refers to. ToolBarDrag Along-axis offsets that open a gap while a toolbar button is dragged. ToolBarEntry Where one toolbar sits. Edge, Band, Index, and Offset stay the last docked place while Floating is set, so a double-click can put it back. PaneId and WindowId name the pane or floating window that hosts it. Both null is the main window. Default values are omitted from JSON. ToolBarItemEntry One customized button. Key is the host's item key. HomeId is the toolbar whose collection owns the item; null means BarId. Items with no entry stay in collection order on their own toolbar. ToolBarItems Ordering and visibility overlay for toolbar buttons. The host collection is not modified. An item with no entry stays on its own toolbar. A new item is inserted after the nearest preceding collection neighbor that is still on that toolbar. Unknown keys are ignored. ToolBarLayout Toolbar bands and button customization stored with a DockLayout. Null on the layout, and omitted from JSON, when the host has no toolbar state. A document written before toolbars existed has no toolBars object and still loads. WorkAreas Places a floating window that lies entirely outside every monitor onto the nearest work area. A window that intersects any work area is left where it is. Coordinates are device-independent pixels, the same space as FloatWindow bounds. Structs AutoHideHit An auto-hide drop. Preview is the strip, or the hot zone when the strip is collapsed. AutoHideStrip One auto-hide strip in the same coordinates as the pointer. Collapsed is an empty strip: the hit test uses HotZoneOf(DockRect, AutoHideEdge) instead of Bounds. DockEditResult Result of a layout edit. Refusals such as "cannot close" do not throw. DockPaneStateChange One pane whose DockPaneState differs between two layouts. DockRect A rectangle in the same coordinate space the host uses for pointer positions. DockTarget A window that can receive a dock drop. WindowId is empty for the main host. A larger ZOrder is painted above a smaller one. RootId is the node edge guides dock against. DragStep What a drag update did to the layout. Structure changes need a view rebuild; a follow only moves a window. TabsMoved means the dragged tab changed slots. The host redraws that strip and does not publish yet. DropGuide A dock target. Root-edge buttons dock against the whole host; other buttons dock against one leaf. NodeBounds Bounds of a leaf tab group, supplied by the view. PaneLocation Where a pane currently lives. Group is null for auto-hidden panes. PlacedPanel A pane located by Build(DockLayout, ISet<string>?) so a host can reattach content by ContentId. ScreenDip A point in device-independent pixels (1/96 inch), the units stored on a FloatWindow. TabStrip.Header One header along the strip. Index is the pane's index in its group. A negative index means this list is the whole group in order, and the list position is the model index. TabStrip.Range Contiguous headers that fit in a strip. First is the model index of the leftmost one. Overflow is true when at least one header is hidden. ToolBarBandRect Arranged bounds of one band. Bands on an edge are passed in band order. ToolBarBarRect Arranged bounds of one docked toolbar, in the same coordinates as the pointer. PaneId and WindowId are empty for a main-window tray. ToolBarDrop A drop target. Float tears the toolbar off. InsertBand opens a new band and shifts bands at Band and after it. Indicator is the line to draw. ToolBarItemRef An item as the host collection currently holds it. ToolBarPackItem One toolbar to place in a band. Offset and Size are along the band. ToolBarSite One place a toolbar can dock. An empty PaneId and WindowId is the main window. A pane id is that pane's content. A window id is a floating window's id. A window with a larger ZOrder is painted above one with a smaller value. OwnerId is the window that shows a pane: empty for the main window, else a floating window's id. ToolBarSlot One slot in a toolbar after the customization overlay is applied. Hidden slots stay in the list. ToolBarTrayRect Arranged bounds of one edge tray. Enums AutoHideEdge Edge of the dock root that holds auto-hidden panes. DockCaptionRole Which caption this bar is. The default template hides the title row on a strip caption. DockGesturePhase Where a DockDragSession is in its gesture. DockKind Document panes live in the document well. Tool panes are tool windows and may auto-hide. DockPaneState Whether a pane is in the main tree, a floating window, an auto-hide strip, or hidden. The first three match PanelPlacement. Hidden is a pane kept in Hidden, which is not a placement the host shows. DockResizeHit Which edge of a floating window a pointer is on. None is the client area. DockResizeMode Whether a splitter, a flyout edge, or a floating window resizes during the drag or on release. DockSide Where a pane is docked relative to an anchor node. DockThemeKind Dark, light, or blue dock chrome. Dark is the default. PanelPlacement Where a pane sits after a layout is applied. SplitOrientation Children of a horizontal split sit left to right. A vertical split stacks them top to bottom. TabPlacement Which edge of a tab group draws the tab strip. ToolBarAlignment Which end of a band a toolbar packs against. Start is the left of a horizontal band and the top of a vertical one. End is the right of a horizontal band and the bottom of a vertical one. Start is the default and is omitted from JSON. ToolBarCustomizationChange What changed in a toolbar or in its buttons. ToolBarEdge Which edge of the dock hosts a toolbar band. A floating toolbar keeps the edge it left.

api/index.html.title: API reference | SmartDock
api/index.html.summary: API reference These pages are generated from the XML comments in the SmartDock and SmartDock.Core assemblies. Both use the SmartDock namespace. SmartDock.Core has the layout tree, DockEdit, DockSerializer, dock-guide hit testing, and the toolbar layout records. It doesn't reference WPF. SmartDock has DockManager, DockCommands, DockTheme, and the chrome controls such as DockTabHeader, DockCaption, DockDropPreview, and DockGuideButton. For how-to guides, start with the articles: Getting started Layout Saving and loading layouts Toolbars Keyboard Themes Events and callbacks

articles/events.html.title: Events and callbacks | SmartDock
articles/events.html.summary: Events and callbacks All events are on DockManager. This handler set cancels closing the "readme" pane and records the rest: public static string? Last { get; private set; } public static void Watch(DockManager dock) { dock.PaneClosing += (_, e) => { if (e.ContentId == "readme") e.Cancel = true; }; dock.PaneClosed += (_, e) => Last = e.ContentId; dock.PaneStateChanged += (_, e) => Last = e.NewState.ToString(); dock.ActivePaneChanged += (_, e) => Last = e.NewContentId; dock.PaneMounted += (_, e) => Last = e.ContentId; dock.PaneUnmounted += (_, e) => Last = e.ContentId; dock.LayoutChanged += (_, _) => Last = "layout"; dock.ToolBarCustomizationChanged += (_, e) => Last = e.ToolBarId; } LayoutChanged Fires after a structural edit, a tab selection change, or a splitter move. Use it to know when to save. Reordering a tab by dragging fires it once, on release. Tearing a pane off into a float fires it as soon as the pane leaves its group. Moving a floating window does not fire it, and neither does a close that a PaneClosing handler cancelled. PaneClosing and PaneClosed PaneClosing fires before a pane is removed, with ContentId and Cancel. Set Cancel to keep the pane; the layout stays as it was and LayoutChanged does not fire. This is where you ask about unsaved changes. It fires for the tab close button, the flyout close button, ClosePane (and so Ctrl+F4), and for a floating window's close button, Alt+F4, or Window.Close. Closing a floating window fires it once for each pane that can close; if any handler cancels, the window stays open and nothing closes. Panes in that window that can't close are docked back without the event, unless they have HideOnClose. A pane with HideOnClose still gets PaneClosing from the same buttons and from ClosePane, but is then hidden rather than removed, so PaneClosed does not fire. PaneClosed fires after a user close has removed the pane. It does not fire when Layout is replaced (including LoadLayout), or for RemovePane, HidePane, ShowPane, or EditLayout; those report PaneStateChanged instead. Closing the host window doesn't fire PaneClosing; it only dismisses the floating windows. PaneStateChanged Fires when a pane moves between Docked, Floating, AutoHidden, and Hidden, with ContentId, OldState, and NewState. Replacing Layout fires it for every pane whose state changed. The state says where the pane is in the layout, not whether its content is on screen. A docked pane in an unselected tab, an auto-hidden pane with its flyout closed, or a float that hasn't placed its content yet has no content in a host. Use PaneMounted and PaneUnmounted for that. ActivePaneChanged Fires when ActiveContentId changes. OldContentId or NewContentId is null when there was, or is, no active pane. The active pane is the one whose tab was selected last or whose content last got keyboard focus. To activate a pane from code, call ActivatePane. It selects the tab of a docked or floating pane, opens an auto-hidden pane's flyout, and shows a hidden pane first. An unknown id does nothing. PaneMounted and PaneUnmounted PaneMounted fires after a pane's content element has been put in a host: the selected tab of a docked group, a floating window, or an open flyout. PaneUnmounted fires after it has been taken out again. The two always alternate for a given content id. Moving content to a different host fires PaneUnmounted, then PaneMounted. If the element stays in the same parent, neither fires, so changing a title or icon doesn't. A selected pane stays mounted as long as its group's view is kept. ToolBarCustomizationChanged Fires after a toolbar button is reordered, moved, hidden, shown, or reset, and when a toolbar is shown or hidden. See Toolbars.

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | SmartDock
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started You need three things: a DockManager in a window, a factory for each content id, and a layout. The manager calls a factory the first time its pane is shown and keeps the control, so moving, floating, or reloading the pane reuses the same instance. Register factories before you assign Layout. A pane shown without a factory gets a "Missing content: id" placeholder, and that placeholder stays cached while the pane is in the layout. The manager starts with no layout, so assign one before the window is shown, or the first frame is empty. <Window x:Class="SmartDock.Docs.Samples.GettingStartedWindow" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:dock="clr-namespace:SmartDock;assembly=SmartDock" Title="SmartDock" Height="640" Width="960"> <dock:DockManager x:Name="Dock" /> </Window> using System.Windows; using System.Windows.Controls; namespace SmartDock.Docs.Samples; public partial class GettingStartedWindow : Window { public GettingStartedWindow() { InitializeComponent(); Dock.RegisterContent("solution", () => new TreeView()); Dock.RegisterContent("program", () => new TextBox()); Dock.RegisterContent("readme", () => new TextBox()); Dock.Layout = DockTree.Create(DockTree.Split("root", SplitOrientation.Horizontal, DockTree.Weighted(0.25, DockTree.Tabs("tools", DockKind.Tool, DockTree.Tool("solution", "Solution Explorer", canClose: false))), DockTree.Weighted(0.75, DockTree.Tabs("docs", DockKind.Document, DockTree.Document("program", "Program.cs"), DockTree.Document("readme", "README.md"))))); } } A horizontal DockTree.Split lays out its children left to right, a vertical one top to bottom. DockTree.Weighted gives a child its weight. DockTree.Tool creates a tool pane that can auto-hide; DockTree.Document creates a document pane that can't. Content ids are case-sensitive and must be unique within a layout. Use the same string in the layout and in RegisterContent. The WPF package pulls in SmartDock.Core. If a project only builds or stores layouts and never shows a window, reference SmartDock.Core alone and use DockTree and DockSerializer from there. Both packages use the SmartDock namespace. Next: Layout and Saving and loading layouts.

articles/keyboard.html.title: Keyboard | SmartDock
articles/keyboard.html.summary: Keyboard Ctrl+Tab Hold Ctrl and press Tab to open the pane switcher. It lists the visible panes, most recently activated first; hidden panes are left out and tools are marked "Tool". With fewer than two panes the key does nothing. The host window and every floating window listen for the key, so it works even when focus is outside the panes. The popup opens over the window that got the key and stays there while you move through the list. The first press highlights the previous pane. Tab or Down moves down the list, Shift+Tab or Up moves back, and the list wraps. Release Ctrl to activate the highlighted pane: its tab is selected, an auto-hidden pane's flyout opens, and a floating pane's window comes to the front. Escape closes the switcher without changing the active pane. The activation order lives in memory only. It is not saved with the layout. Commands DockCommands has routed commands that DockManager already handles. Their default keys are in each command's InputGestures, which is read on every key press, so a change takes effect immediately. Command Default key What it does ClosePane Ctrl+F4 Closes the active pane. A pane with HideOnClose is hidden instead of removed. NextDocument Ctrl+PageDown Activates the next document tab. PreviousDocument Ctrl+PageUp Activates the previous document tab. ToggleFloat none Floats the active pane, or docks a floating pane back. ToggleAutoHide none Auto-hides the active tool, or pins a tool that is already on an auto-hide strip. public static void Run(DockManager dock) { DockCommands.ClosePane.Execute(null, dock); DockCommands.NextDocument.Execute(null, dock); DockCommands.PreviousDocument.Execute(null, dock); DockCommands.ToggleFloat.Execute(null, dock); DockCommands.ToggleAutoHide.Execute(null, dock); } ToggleFloat opens the float at (80, 80), 480 by 360, if the pane is allowed to float, and docks a pane that is already floating back. ToggleAutoHide does nothing when the active pane can't auto-hide. To rebind a command, replace its gestures: public static void RebindClose() { DockCommands.ClosePane.InputGestures.Clear(); DockCommands.ClosePane.InputGestures.Add(new KeyGesture(Key.W, ModifierKeys.Control)); } DockCommands is static, so this changes the key for every DockManager in the process.

articles/layout.html.title: Layout | SmartDock
articles/layout.html.summary: Layout A DockLayout holds the main tree, the floating windows, four auto-hide strips, and any hidden panes. You change it with DockEdit. Each call returns a DockEditResult instead of throwing: a refused edit leaves the tree as it was, and a tree produced by a successful structural edit is valid to save. Splits and tabs You can build the tree in code or declare it in XAML. In XAML you need two prefixes: the controls live in the SmartDock assembly and the model types in SmartDock.Core, both under the SmartDock namespace. Factories still have to be registered before Layout is set. DockManager is sealed, so you can't do that in a subclass constructor. This sample uses an attached property instead: XAML applies attributes on the start tag before property elements, so Prepare runs before the Layout element is assigned. using System.Windows; using System.Windows.Controls; namespace SmartDock.Docs.Samples; public static class SampleContent { public static readonly DependencyProperty PrepareProperty = DependencyProperty.RegisterAttached( "Prepare", typeof(bool), typeof(SampleContent), new PropertyMetadata(false, OnPrepare)); public static void SetPrepare(DependencyObject element, bool value) => element.SetValue(PrepareProperty, value); public static bool GetPrepare(DependencyObject element) => (bool)element.GetValue(PrepareProperty); private static void OnPrepare(DependencyObject element, DependencyPropertyChangedEventArgs args) { if (element is not DockManager dock || args.NewValue is not true) return; dock.RegisterContent("solution", () => new TreeView()); dock.RegisterContent("properties", () => new TextBox()); dock.RegisterContent("program", () => new TextBox()); dock.RegisterContent("readme", () => new TextBox()); } } <Window x:Class="SmartDock.Docs.Samples.LayoutWindow" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:dock="clr-namespace:SmartDock;assembly=SmartDock" xmlns:local="clr-namespace:SmartDock.Docs.Samples" xmlns:model="clr-namespace:SmartDock;assembly=SmartDock.Core" Title="SmartDock" Height="640" Width="960"> <dock:DockManager local:SampleContent.Prepare="True"> <dock:DockManager.Layout> <model:DockLayout> <model:DockLayout.Root> <model:SplitNode Id="root" Orientation="Horizontal"> <model:SplitNode.Children> <model:SplitChild Proportion="0.25"> <model:SplitChild.Node> <model:TabGroupNode Id="tools" Kind="Tool"> <model:TabGroupNode.Panels> <model:DockPane ContentId="solution" Title="Solution Explorer" Kind="Tool" CanClose="False" CanAutoHide="True" /> <model:DockPane ContentId="properties" Title="Properties" Kind="Tool" /> </model:TabGroupNode.Panels> </model:TabGroupNode> </model:SplitChild.Node> </model:SplitChild> <model:SplitChild Proportion="0.75"> <model:SplitChild.Node> <model:TabGroupNode Id="docs" Kind="Document"> <model:TabGroupNode.Panels> <model:DockPane ContentId="program" Title="Program.cs" /> <model:DockPane ContentId="readme" Title="README.md" /> </model:TabGroupNode.Panels> </model:TabGroupNode> </model:SplitChild.Node> </model:SplitChild> </model:SplitNode.Children> </model:SplitNode> </model:DockLayout.Root> </model:DockLayout> </dock:DockManager.Layout> </dock:DockManager> </Window> Proportion is a positive weight. The weights don't need to add up to 1. A tool pane can auto-hide only when CanAutoHide is true. DockTree.Tool sets it for you, but a DockPane declared in XAML leaves it false unless you set it. TabGroupNode.SelectedIndex is the selected tab, and it is saved with the layout. DockManager.TabPlacement (tool groups) and DocumentTabPlacement (document groups) put the tab strip above or below the content. Both default to Top. The same tree in code: public static DockLayout Build() { return DockTree.Create(DockTree.Split("root", SplitOrientation.Horizontal, DockTree.Weighted(0.25, DockTree.Tabs("tools", DockKind.Tool, DockTree.Tool("solution", "Solution Explorer", canClose: false), DockTree.Tool("properties", "Properties"))), DockTree.Weighted(0.75, DockTree.Tabs("docs", DockKind.Document, DockTree.Document("program", "Program.cs"), DockTree.Document("readme", "README.md"))))); } Docking DockEdit.Dock moves a pane that is already in the layout. DockSide.Left, Right, Top, and Bottom split the anchor and give the pane DockEdit.DefaultProportion (0.25) unless you pass another weight. DockSide.Center adds the pane as a tab, so the anchor has to be a tab group. On a live manager, call DockManager.DockPaneTo. It runs the same edit and raises LayoutChanged if the tree changed. Floating windows DockEdit.Float takes a pane out of the tree and puts it in a new floating window at the bounds you pass, in device-independent pixels. DockEdit.DockBack puts it back: into the tab group it came from if that group still exists, otherwise into the first main-tree group of the same kind, otherwise into a new group on the right. A floating window can be saved maximized. Its x, y, width, and height are then the restored bounds, not the maximized ones. DockManager.FloatPane and DockManager.DockBackPane do the same on a live manager. A floating window draws its own caption. Drag the caption to move the window, or drop it on a guide to dock the whole window. Double-clicking the caption docks the selected pane back if its previous group is still in the main tree, and maximizes the window otherwise. Auto-hide DockEdit.AutoHide moves a tool onto an auto-hide strip on one edge of the dock root. The pane must have CanAutoHide set. DockEdit.Pin docks it back. A new auto-hide entry gets a flyout size of 240 device-independent pixels. public static void Move(DockLayout layout) { DockEdit.Dock(layout, "readme", "docs", DockSide.Right); DockEdit.Float(layout, "readme", 80, 60, 480, 320); DockEdit.DockBack(layout, "readme"); DockEdit.AutoHide(layout, "solution", AutoHideEdge.Left); DockEdit.Pin(layout, "solution"); DockEdit.Select(layout, "program"); } DockManager.AutoHidePane and DockManager.PinPane do the same on a live manager. The flyout is a native child window of the dock, so it paints above HwndHost content in other panes. Because it is a separate window, it opens at full size instead of sliding in. Drag and drop guides Drag a tab along its strip to reorder it. Drag it off the strip to float the pane, then release over a guide to dock it. While you drag, the dock shows a compass over the tab group under the pointer and one button at the middle of each edge of the host. A compass side button splits that leaf in half. The preview shows the same slice the drop inserts. The compass center button adds the pane as a tab of that group. An edge button docks against the root and takes one quarter of the host. A root-edge button wins when it overlaps the compass. A tool, or a float made of tools, can also drop on an auto-hide strip. A document has no auto-hide target. When the pointer is over another floating window, that window's compass and edge buttons are shown. The topmost window wins, and the window being dragged is skipped. Guides and the drop preview are drawn in a topmost overlay, so the window you drag never covers them. Dropping a single torn-off pane calls DockEdit.Dock. Dropping a whole window calls DockEdit.DockWindow: a side button keeps the window's tree as it is, and the center button appends its panes to the target group. Hide and show DockEdit.Hide takes a pane out of the tree and stores it on DockLayout.Hidden, along with the place DockEdit.Show puts it back. Hiding works even when CanClose is false. A hidden pane isn't drawn and doesn't appear in the Ctrl+Tab switcher. On a live manager, use DockManager.HidePane and DockManager.ShowPane. Events and callbacks lists the events a hide raises.

articles/saving-layouts.html.title: Saving and loading layouts | SmartDock
articles/saving-layouts.html.summary: Saving and loading layouts DockSerializer turns a layout into one line of compact JSON and back. The format version is DockLayout.CurrentVersion, currently 1. Serialize validates the tree before writing. Deserialize throws DockLayoutException when the JSON is malformed or the tree fails validation. That covers a version other than 1, a missing or repeated id, a split with fewer than two children, an empty tab group that no hidden entry points to, and a non-finite number where a finite one is required. A round trip is exact: a document written by Serialize reads back as an equal layout and writes out as the same bytes. The file keeps ids, weights, the selected tab, float bounds and the maximized flag, auto-hide entries, hidden panes, and toolbar state. When DockLayout.ToolBars is null, the file has no toolBars object at all. Enums are written as lowercase strings, and each node has "type": "split" or "type": "tabs". public static string CoreRoundTrip(DockLayout layout) { string json = DockSerializer.Serialize(layout); DockLayout restored = DockSerializer.Deserialize(json); return DockSerializer.Serialize(restored); } With a DockManager, use SaveLayout and LoadLayout. SaveLayout copies the current toolbar positions into the layout before it serializes, and throws InvalidOperationException when no layout is assigned. LoadLayout deserializes and assigns Layout. Call it before the window is shown, or while the manager is hidden, so the first frame on screen is the saved layout. Loading raises PaneStateChanged for panes whose state changed. It never raises PaneClosing or PaneClosed. public static void ManagerRoundTrip(DockManager dock, string path) { File.WriteAllText(path, dock.SaveLayout()); dock.LoadLayout(File.ReadAllText(path)); } DockSerializer.SerializeUtf8 writes the same document as UTF-8 bytes. DockLayout.Clone makes a deep copy through the same JSON and also copies DockPane.PreviousGroupId, which the file doesn't store. The theme, the Ctrl+Tab activation order, and pane icons are not saved. Restore them yourself if you need them.

articles/themes.html.title: Themes | SmartDock
articles/themes.html.summary: Themes Set DockManager.Theme to DockThemeKind.Dark (the default), Light, or Blue. The new brushes replace the old ones in the manager, its floating windows, the guide overlay, the pane switcher, and the auto-hide flyout, and everything repaints in place. The theme is not saved with the layout. public static void UseLight(DockManager dock) { dock.Theme = DockThemeKind.Light; } To use the dock palette outside the manager, for example in a dictionary merged into Application.Resources, call DockTheme.Apply on any FrameworkElement or ResourceDictionary. public static void ApplyBlue(FrameworkElement element) { DockTheme.Apply(element, DockThemeKind.Blue); } The chrome looks brushes up by resource key, not through the static brush properties. The keys are Dock.Workspace, Dock.Panel, Dock.Chrome, Dock.Header, Dock.Border, Dock.Text, Dock.Muted, Dock.Accent, Dock.AccentSoft, Dock.Guide, Dock.GuideButton, Dock.GuideBorder, Dock.Hover, and Dock.Font. DockTheme exposes each name as a *Key constant, for example DockTheme.WorkspaceKey. The static brushes on DockTheme always hold the dark palette, and the chrome doesn't use them. Don't reference DockTheme.Border or DockTheme.Panel with x:Static: those names match WPF types, and the markup compiler resolves them as types. DockTheme.CreateScrollBarResources returns styles for the scroll bar, tool tip, and focus visual. The manager, each floating window, and the switcher merge it already. Merge your own copy if you want the same scroll bars elsewhere in the app. DockTheme.CreateMenuResources returns menu, context menu, menu item, and separator styles in the dock colors. Nothing merges it for you. Merge it into application resources if your menus should match the dock, or leave it out to keep the system look. A copy merged into the host window follows Theme changes.

articles/toolbars.html.title: Toolbars | SmartDock
articles/toolbars.html.summary: Toolbars Put ordinary WPF ToolBar controls in DockManager.ToolBars and the dock lays them out in trays on the main window, on a floating window, or on a pane. If you never touch ToolBars or ToolBarsSource, no tray is built. Set DockToolBar attached properties on each toolbar to say where it goes: Property Meaning Id Stable id. A saved entry is matched to the toolbar by this string. The toolbar's Name is used when Id is empty. Title Caption of a floating toolbar, and the label in the tray menu. Edge Top, Bottom, Left, or Right. The default is Top. Band Row or column on that edge. Band 0 is the outer side: the top of a top tray, the bottom of a bottom tray, the left of a left tray, and the right of a right tray. BandIndex Position within the band. Offset Gap before the toolbar, in device-independent pixels. Alignment Start packs from the left of a horizontal band or the top of a vertical one. End packs from the right or the bottom. Start is the default. PaneId Content id of the pane that hosts the toolbar. Empty means a window tray. A pane that is not in the layout uses the main window's top tray. IsVisible False hides the toolbar and keeps a floating window's bounds. True shows it again. ShowOverflow When true, the toolbar uses the leftover space in the band and shows an overflow chevron. The default is false. IsCustomizable When false, that toolbar has no customize menu and ignores Alt+drag. The default is true. Edge, Band, BandIndex, Offset, Alignment, and PaneId only set the starting place. Once the toolbar has been shown or dragged, its layout entry decides where it is, and changing these properties no longer moves it. <Window x:Class="SmartDock.Docs.Samples.ToolbarWindow" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:dock="clr-namespace:SmartDock;assembly=SmartDock" Title="SmartDock" Height="640" Width="960"> <dock:DockManager x:Name="Dock"> <dock:DockManager.ToolBars> <ToolBar dock:DockToolBar.Id="standard" dock:DockToolBar.Title="Standard" dock:DockToolBar.Edge="Top" dock:DockToolBar.Band="0" dock:DockToolBar.Alignment="Start"> <Button Content="Save" /> </ToolBar> </dock:DockManager.ToolBars> </dock:DockManager> </Window> The same thing in code: public static void AddAligned(DockManager dock) { var bar = new ToolBar(); DockToolBar.SetId(bar, "standard"); DockToolBar.SetTitle(bar, "Standard"); DockToolBar.SetEdge(bar, ToolBarEdge.Top); DockToolBar.SetBand(bar, 0); DockToolBar.SetBandIndex(bar, 0); DockToolBar.SetOffset(bar, 0); DockToolBar.SetAlignment(bar, ToolBarAlignment.End); bar.Items.Add(new Button { Name = "save", Content = "Save" }); dock.ToolBars.Add(bar); DockToolBar.SetIsVisible(bar, false); DockToolBar.SetIsVisible(bar, true); dock.ToolBarCustomizationEnabled = true; } To bind toolbars from view models, use ToolBarsSource. Each item becomes a ToolBar built from ToolBarTemplateSelector if set, else ToolBarTemplate, else the implicit data template. Placement comes from DockToolBarItem instead of the attached properties: bind its properties in a style assigned to ToolBarItemStyle. The buttons themselves stay in each toolbar's own Items or ItemsSource. Floating toolbars Drag the grip along the band to slide the toolbar. Drag it out of the tray and it turns into a floating window that follows the pointer; release to leave it there. Moving back over a tray in the same drag docks it again. Double-click the grip of a floating toolbar to send it back to the band it came from. The close button on the caption hides the toolbar, and showing it again reopens the window at the same bounds. A toolbar with PaneId set travels with its pane when the pane floats, docks somewhere else, changes tabs, or auto-hides. When the pane closes, the toolbar goes back to its declared place. Customize menu and hide or show Users can customize toolbars unless you turn it off. ToolBarCustomizationEnabled is true by default. Right-click an empty part of a tray to get a menu of all toolbars, listed by title (or id when the title is empty). Visible ones are checked; uncheck one to hide it. The customize button on a toolbar opens "Add or Remove Buttons". Every button with a stable key has a check item there; uncheck it to hide the button. Reset undoes all button changes on that toolbar. Alt+drag a button to reorder it, move it to another toolbar, or drop it outside the toolbars to hide it. Customization is saved per button key. The key is DockToolBar.Key if set. Otherwise it comes from ToolBarItemKeyPath, then the element's Name, ContentId, Id, or a string ToolTip or ToolTipText. A button with none of these gets a key for the current session only: its changes are not saved, and it doesn't appear in the customize menu. Give your buttons names or keys. Set ToolBarCustomizationEnabled to false to turn off Alt+drag, the customize menu, and the tray menu everywhere. Set IsCustomizable to false to do the same for one toolbar. By default the dock keeps the user's button order as an overlay and leaves your item collections alone. Set ToolBarMoveItemsInSource to true if a reorder or a move between toolbars should edit the source lists too. Only do that when those lists are writable. ToolBarCustomizationChanged fires after a button is reordered, moved, hidden, shown, or reset, and when a whole toolbar is shown or hidden. ToolBarId names the toolbar. ItemKey is the button's key, or null when the change is about the toolbar itself. FromToolBarId is set when a button came from another toolbar. Layout persistence DockManager.SaveLayout writes bands, alignment, floating bounds, visibility, and button order to DockLayout.ToolBars, and LoadLayout restores them. A file without a toolBars object loads fine. See Saving and loading layouts.

index.html.title: SmartDock | SmartDock
index.html.summary: SmartDock SmartDock is a docking library for WPF on .NET 8. A layout is a tree of splits and tab groups. Every pane has a stable content id, and when a layout is shown or restored, the dock maps each id back to your control. There are two packages, both in the SmartDock namespace: SmartDock is the WPF part. DockManager draws the splits, tabs, floating windows, auto-hide strips, and toolbars. SmartDock.Core has the layout model, the edit operations, and the JSON serializer. It doesn't reference WPF, so a service or a command-line tool can build and save layouts too. Features Horizontal and vertical splits. Proportions are weights and do not have to sum to 1. Document and tool tab groups. Only the selected tab's content is in the visual tree. Dock a pane to the left, right, top, or bottom of an anchor, or add it as a tab. Floating windows with their own captions. They can be maximized and docked back. Auto-hide strips and flyouts for tool panes that allow it. Drag a tab along its strip to reorder it, or off the strip to float it, then drop it on a dock guide. Hide a pane and show it again later. A hidden pane stays in the saved layout. Save and load the whole layout as compact JSON, including floats, auto-hide, hidden panes, and toolbars. Toolbars on the main window, on floating windows, and on panes, with a customize menu. Their positions are saved with the layout. A Ctrl+Tab pane switcher, plus commands for close, document cycling, float, and auto-hide. Dark, light, and blue chrome. Dark is the default. Events for layout changes, closing, pane state, activation, and when a pane's content is mounted or unmounted. Bind documents and tools to a collection, with a data template per item. Install dotnet add package SmartDock --version 0.9.0 It pulls in SmartDock.Core. If you only build or store layouts, the core package is enough: dotnet add package SmartDock.Core --version 0.9.0 The WPF package needs net8.0-windows. SmartDock.Core targets plain net8.0. Read next Getting started Layout Saving and loading layouts Toolbars Keyboard Themes Events and callbacks API reference Issues Report bugs and API questions at https://github.com/ArcticNoise/SmartDock/issues.
